{"findings": [{"file": "src/completion_queue.zig", "line": 320, "severity": "major", "category": "correctness", "title": "getResult now reports error.Closed on an open queue, and no caller can tell it apart from a real drain", "body": "The change removes the assert and returns `error.Closed` for a wake that lands with the queue EMPTY and OPEN. `error.Closed` is defined by this file as "closed and fully drained" (module doc lines 45-48, `wait` doc line 174, protocol comment line 283). The select arm now returns that error while the queue is open and operations are still in flight.

Mechanism: a stale wake wins the select arm; `completed.pop()` returns null; the function returns `error.Closed` without reading `self.closed` or `self.pending` at all. The caller sees the same value it sees after a real drain.

Consequence: a caller that follows the documented dispatcher loop (`error.Closed => break`, module doc line 42) tears the driver down while the queue is open. Every operation still in `pending` is abandoned. For the heap-backed operations that the module doc requires other tasks to submit (lines 14-20), the driver is the only owner, so those allocations leak.

The comment tells the caller to "know it never closed the queue" and re-poll. That instruction is not satisfiable through the public API: there is no `isClosed()` accessor, and `close()` is documented as thread-safe, so another task can close the queue at any time. `isEmpty()`/`hasPending()` return true for both the spurious case and the real drained case. So the caller cannot implement the workaround the comment prescribes.

A fix that keeps the contract: read the drained state under the same mutex, and give the spurious case its own outcome the type can express (widen `Result`, or make the select arm re-park instead of deciding). Note also that the removed assert was the only detector for the upstream protocol bug this comment describes; nothing replaces it in any build mode, so the bug is now silent everywhere."}, {"file": "src/completion_queue.zig", "line": 86, "severity": "major", "category": "docs", "title": "The file still states the strict wake invariant that this change abandons", "body": "The change makes a wake on `signal` able to reach the select arm with nothing to report, but three places in the same file still state the opposite invariant, and one of them is the user-facing example.

1. Line 84-86, the `signal` field doc: "The future protocol depends on the strict reading of a wake: a completion is takeable, or the queue is drained." The new comment in `getResult` says this reading no longer holds.
2. Line 279-281, the future protocol comment: "The registered wait completes when a completion is ready to be taken or the queue is drained." A stale wake now completes it in a third state.
3. Line 52-57, the module doc for the select path: "The winning result is what `wait` would have returned." On the new path `wait` would have blocked; the select arm returns `error.Closed`.

The module doc example at lines 40-49 also still shows `error.Closed => break` as the correct handling, which is now the wrong action for a select-based driver.

Consequence: a reader of the public documentation writes the teardown that the new comment inside the private function warns against. The two statements contradict each other and only one of them reaches the user."}, {"file": "src/completion_queue.zig", "line": 302, "severity": "minor", "category": "tests", "title": "No test pins the new spurious-Closed behavior of getResult", "body": "The change replaces a `std.debug.assert` with a returned value, and adds no test. The file has a large select test block (lines 1112-1311), including one that pins the real drained case ("select on a drained queue reports error.Closed"), but nothing covers the new case.

`asyncWait`, `asyncCancelWait`, `getResult` and `WaitContext` are all public, so the new behavior is testable directly and cheaply: build a `WaitContext`, call `getResult` on an open empty queue, and assert `error.Closed` rather than a crash.

Consequence: a later change that restores the assert, or that makes `getResult` read `self.closed` again, passes the whole suite in every build mode. The behavior this commit exists to create has no regression guard."}]}
